"'''Thrift Shop'''" is a song written and performed by American [[hip hop music|hip hop]] duo [[Macklemore & Ryan Lewis]]. It was released in 2012 as the fourth single from the pair's debut studio album ''[[The Heist (album)|The Heist]]'' (2012), and features vocals from American singer [[Wanz]]. The lyrics tell of Macklemore's esteem for going to thrift shops and saving money, rather than flaunting expensive items like many rappers. The song was met with universal acclaim, with various music reviewers praising its humorous lyrics and [[social critique]].

Despite being released on Macklemore's [[independent record label]] with distribution by the [[Alternative Distribution Alliance|Alternative Distribution Alliance (ADA)]], a [[Warner Music Group]] company, the single was a [[sleeper hit]]. It reached number one on the US [[Billboard Hot 100|''Billboard'' Hot 100]] and has since sold over 6 million copies in the US alone.<ref name="2013yearsales">{{cite magazine |last1=Caulfield |first1=Keith |title=Justin Timberlake's '20/18' 2011's Best Selling Album, 'Blurred Lines' Top Song |url=https://www.billboard.com/articles/news/5855151/justin-timberlakes-2018-2011s-best-selling-album-blurred-lines-top-song |magazine=Billboard |access-date=31 July 2017 |date=2 January 2012}}</ref> The song also reached number one in the United Kingdom, Ireland, Canada, France, Denmark, Netherlands, Australia and New Zealand. The song would go on to become the [[Billboard Year-End Hot 100 singles of 2013|number one song of 2013]] by ''[[Billboard (magazine)|Billboard]]'' and in 2019, it was named by ''Billboard'' as the number one song of the 2010s on both the [[Hot Rap Songs]] and the [[Hot R&B/Hip-Hop Songs]] charts.

A music video was released simultaneously with the song on August 29, 2012, and has more than 1.9 billion views on YouTube as of February 2025. At the [[56th Annual Grammy Awards]] in 2014, the single won for [[Grammy Award for Best Rap Performance|Best Rap Performance]] and [[Grammy Award for Best Rap Song|Best Rap Song]].<ref>{{cite magazine|url=http://www.billboard.com/articles/news/5819883/grammy-awards-2012-full-nominations-list-complete-nominees |title=Grammy Awards 2012: Full Nominations List |magazine=[[Billboard (magazine)|Billboard]] |date=December 6, 2011 |access-date=March 23, 2012}}</ref>

"Thrift Shop" is a song written and performed by American hip hop duo Macklemore & Ryan Lewis. It was released in 2012 as the fourth single from the pair's debut studio album The Heist (2012), and features vocals from American singer Wanz. The lyrics tell of Macklemore's esteem for going to thrift shops and saving money, rather than flaunting expensive items like many rappers. The song was met with universal acclaim, with various music reviewers praising its humorous lyrics and social critique.

Despite being released on Macklemore's independent record label with distribution by the Alternative Distribution Alliance (ADA), a Warner Music Group company, the single was a sleeper hit. It reached number one on the US Billboard Hot 100 and has since sold over 6 million copies in the US alone. The song also reached number one in the United Kingdom, Ireland, Canada, France, Denmark, Netherlands, Australia and New Zealand. The song would go on to become the number one song of 2013 by Billboard and in 2019, it was named by Billboard as the number one song of the 2010s on both the Hot Rap Songs and the Hot R&B/Hip-Hop Songs charts.

A music video was released simultaneously with the song on August 29, 2012, and has more than 1.9 billion views on YouTube as of February 2025. At the 56th Annual Grammy Awards in 2014, the single won for Best Rap Performance and Best Rap Song.

sections.heading: Background and composition
sections.wikitext:
The song illustrates Macklemore's interest in buying cheap clothing from thrift shops, disdaining [[designer label]]s and trends. He claims to enjoy donning "your granddad's clothes" and impulsively buying a sharp-looking but strong-smelling fur [[Stole (shawl)|stole]] just because "it was 99 cents". Macklemore spoke to MTV News about the meaning of the song. "Rappers talk about, oh I buy this and I buy that, and I spend this much money and I make it rain, and this type of champagne and painting the club, and this is the kind of record that's the exact opposite," he explained. "It's the polar opposite of it. It's kind of standing for like let's save some money, let's keep some money away, let's spend as little as possible and look as fresh as possible at the same time."<ref name="ibtimes" />

Asked why he thought the track was so successful, Macklemore replied, "I think hip-hop goes in waves, and it's something that's different. It's a concept. It's obviously against the status quo of what people normally rap about. This is a song that goes against all of that. How much can you save? How fresh can you look by not looking like anybody else? And on top of that, you have an infectious beat and a hook that gets stuck in people's heads."<ref>{{cite web|url=http://m.mtv.com/news/article.rbml?id=1700851 |archive-url=https://archive.today/20131202051850/http://m.mtv.com/news/article.rbml?id=1700851 |url-status=dead |archive-date=December 2, 2013 |title=Macklemore 'Never' Thought 'Thrift Shop' Would Hit #1|website=[[MTV]]|access-date=December 2, 2013}}</ref>

Macklemore stated that the message he was trying to send with that song was: "Don't be a fuckboy and think that a logo is going to make you cool. There are finds out there. There are treasures. There are amazing ways that you can freak fashion and be an individual, and we don't need to get caught up spending all this money. Save it. Go to the thrift shop."<ref>[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=4C-mR-0X0Yw Macklemore – The Making of 'Thrift Shop' (Vevo Footnotes)]</ref>

"Thrift Shop" is written in the key of [[G-sharp minor|G{{music|sharp}} minor]] and has a [[tempo]] of 95 beats per minute.<ref>{{cite web|author=Wanz |url=http://www.musicnotes.com/sheetmusic/mtdFPE.asp?ppn=MN0118875& |title=Macklemore "Thrift Shop" Sheet Music – Download & Print |website=Musicnotes.com | date=June 11, 2013 |access-date=2013-06-20}}</ref> The song is prominently underpinned by a looping saxophone melody.<ref name="triplej">{{cite web |date=26 February 2013 |author=Jadey O'Regan |title=Behind 'Thrift Shop': What made it a Triple J hit?|url=http://www.fasterlouder.com.au/features/35029/Behind-Thrift-Shop-What-made-it-a-triple-j-hit |website=FasterLouder.com.au |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130301061101/http://www.fasterlouder.com.au/features/35029/Behind-Thrift-Shop-What-made-it-a-triple-j-hit |archive-date=2013-03-01 }}</ref>

sections.heading: Critical reception
Chart performance
sections.wikitext:
In the United States, the song debuted on the [[Billboard Hot 100|''Billboard'' Hot 100]] on September 15, 2012. It dropped out the following week but re-entered five weeks later on October 20. The song then steadily climbed the chart until it entered the top ten in the issue dated January 5, 2013. It replaced Bruno Mars' "[[Locked Out of Heaven]]" at number one in its 16th week on the chart on February 2, 2013{{cite magazine|url=http://www.billboard.com/articles/news/1521657/macklemore-ryan-lewis-crown-hot-100-justin-timberlake-soars-to-top-5|title=Macklemore & Ryan Lewis Crown Hot 100, Justin Timberlake Soars to Top 5|last=Trust|first=Gary|magazine=[[Billboard (magazine)|Billboard]]|access-date=February 12, 2013}} and remained atop the chart for six non-consecutive weeks.{{cite magazine|url=https://www.billboard.com/pro/macklemore-ryan-lewis-return-to-top-of-hot-100/|title=Macklemore & Ryan Lewis Return To Top Of Hot 100|last=Trust|first=Gary|magazine=Billboard|access-date=2013-03-27}} It also topped the [[Hot Rap Songs|Rap Songs]] chart for fifteen weeks. "Thrift Shop" was the second best-selling single of 2013 in the US after [[Robin Thicke]]'s "[[Blurred Lines]]", with 6,148,000 copies sold during the year.{{cite news |url=http://music.yahoo.com/blogs/music-news/chart-watch-top-10-albums-songs-2013-184702481.html |title=The Top 10 Albums and Songs of 2013 | first= Paul | last= Grein |date=January 2, 2014 |work=Chart Watch |publisher=Yahoo }} As of November 2015, the song has sold 7,740,000 downloads in the United States, making it the fifth-best selling digital single in the country ever.{{cite web |url=http://hitsdailydouble.com/news&id=295457 |title=The Rise of Uptown Funk: Could It Become the All-Time #1 Seller? |website=[[Hits (magazine)|HITS Daily Double]] |publisher=HITS Digital Ventures |date=April 9, 2015 |access-date=April 9, 2015}} The song also had much success on [[Billboard (magazine)|''Billboard'']]'s component charts, remaining atop the [[Hot Digital Songs|Digital Songs]] chart for ten weeks and topping ''Billboard''{{'}}s [[Hot 100 Airplay|Radio Songs]] chart for two weeks. It also peaked at number one on the On-Demand Songs chart and remained there for eleven weeks until the week ending March 30, 2013. It set a record on that chart as the first song to reach two million streams in a single week since the chart's inception. The song also topped the [[Hot R&B/Hip-Hop Songs|R&B/Hip-Hop Songs]] chart for fourteen consecutive weeks. The song was the first independently distributed title to top the ''Billboard'' [[Hot Digital Songs|Digital Songs]] since "[[We Are the World 25 for Haiti]]" in February 2010. It was also only the second independent song to reach number one on the ''Billboard'' Hot 100 chart, nearly 20 years after [[Lisa Loeb]]'s "[[Stay (I Missed You)]]" in 1994.{{cite magazine |last=Feeney |first=Nolan |date=January 25, 2013 |title=Macklemore's 'Thrift Shop' Is First Indie Hit to Top Charts in Nearly Two Decades |url=https://newsfeed.time.com/2013/01/25/macklemores-thrift-shop-is-first-indie-hit-to-top-charts-in-nearly-two-decades/ |magazine=[[Time (magazine)|Time]] |access-date=December 2, 2013}} ''Billboard'' ranked it as the No. 1 song for 2013.[[Billboard Year-End Hot 100 singles of 2013]] In the United Kingdom, "Thrift Shop" entered the [[UK Singles Chart]] at number twenty-four in late January 2013, despite having been available as a single via [[iTunes]] since August 1, 2012. The following week, the single rose twenty-two positions to number two. Two weeks after entering the chart, the song reached number one on February 10, 2013 ― for the week ending date February 16, 2013 ― making Macklemore and Ryan Lewis only the second act to have a number one in Britain with a self-released single.{{cite web |url=http://www.officialcharts.com/chart-news/thrift-shop-checks-out-at-number-1-1849/ |title=Thrift Shop checks out at Number 1/ |work=[[UK Singles Chart]] |publisher=[[Official Charts Company]] |access-date=February 10, 2013 }}
- {{cite web | url=http://top40.about.com/od/onthecharts/a/Uk-Pop-Charts-For-Week-Ending-February-16-2013.htm | title=UK Pop Charts for Week Ending February 16, 2013 | author=Masterton, James | author-link=James Masterton | work=About.com | publisher=[[IAC (company)|InterActiveCorp]] | access-date=December 2, 2013 | archive-date=December 3, 2013 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131203061125/http://top40.about.com/od/onthecharts/a/Uk-Pop-Charts-For-Week-Ending-February-16-2013.htm | url-status=dead }} As of July 2013, "Thrift Shop" has sold 680,000 copies in the UK.{{cite web|url=http://www.officialcharts.com/chart-news/the-official-top-40-biggest-selling-singles-and-albums-of-2013-so-far2-2328/|title=The Official Top 40 Biggest Selling Singles And Albums Of 2013 So Far!|last=Lane|first=Daniel|publisher=[[Official Charts Company]]|date=July 3, 2013|access-date=July 3, 2013}} In Canada, the song topped the [[Canadian Hot 100]] for six consecutive weeks.{{cite web|url=http://www.billboard.com/biz/articles/news/chart-alert/1555889/macklemore-ryan-lewis-top-hot-100-imagine-dragons-ariana|title=Macklemore & Ryan Lewis Top Hot 100; Imagine Dragons, Ariana Grande Hit Top 10|last=Trust|first=Gary|work=[[Billboard Hot 100|Billboard]]|date=April 3, 2013|access-date=June 17, 2013}} It was the country's second best-selling digital song of 2013 with 554,000 copies sold (all versions combined).{{cite magazine|url=http://www.billboard.com/biz/articles/news/record-labels/5869529/canadas-digital-music-sales-rise-in-2013-unlike-the-us|title=Canada's Digital Music Sales Rise in 2013 Unlike the U.S.; Eminem, Robin Thicke Among Top Selling Artists|last=Bliss|first=Karen|date=January 10, 2014|access-date=January 11, 2014|magazine=Billboard}}

In the United States, the song debuted on the Billboard Hot 100 on September 15, 2012. It dropped out the following week but re-entered five weeks later on October 20. The song then steadily climbed the chart until it entered the top ten in the issue dated January 5, 2013. It replaced Bruno Mars' "Locked Out of Heaven" at number one in its 16th week on the chart on February 2, 2013 and remained atop the chart for six non-consecutive weeks. It also topped the Rap Songs chart for fifteen weeks. "Thrift Shop" was the second best-selling single of 2013 in the US after Robin Thicke's "Blurred Lines", with 6,148,000 copies sold during the year. As of November 2015, the song has sold 7,740,000 downloads in the United States, making it the fifth-best selling digital single in the country ever.

The song also had much success on Billboards component charts, remaining atop the Digital Songs chart for ten weeks and topping Billboard{{'}}s Radio Songs chart for two weeks. It also peaked at number one on the On-Demand Songs chart and remained there for eleven weeks until the week ending March 30, 2013. It set a record on that chart as the first song to reach two million streams in a single week since the chart's inception. The song also topped the R&B/Hip-Hop Songs chart for fourteen consecutive weeks. The song was the first independently distributed title to top the Billboard Digital Songs since "We Are the World 25 for Haiti" in February 2010. It was also only the second independent song to reach number one on the Billboard Hot 100 chart, nearly 20 years after Lisa Loeb's "Stay (I Missed You)" in 1994. Billboard ranked it as the No. 1 song for 2013.

In the United Kingdom, "Thrift Shop" entered the UK Singles Chart at number twenty-four in late January 2013, despite having been available as a single via iTunes since August 1, 2012. The following week, the single rose twenty-two positions to number two. Two weeks after entering the chart, the song reached number one on February 10, 2013 ― for the week ending date February 16, 2013 ― making Macklemore and Ryan Lewis only the second act to have a number one in Britain with a self-released single. As of July 2013, "Thrift Shop" has sold 680,000 copies in the UK.

In Canada, the song topped the Canadian Hot 100 for six consecutive weeks. It was the country's second best-selling digital song of 2013 with 554,000 copies sold (all versions combined).

sections.heading: Wider reception
sections.wikitext:
In August 2013, the rapper [[Le1f]] publicly criticized Macklemore's song on Twitter, claiming that "Thrift Shop" borrowed its beat extensively from his own earlier song, "Wut".{{cite web |title=That Time Macklemore Stole "Thrift Shop" From A Queer New York Rapper |author=Tharrett, Matthew |date=August 27, 2013 |website=Queerty |url=http://www.queerty.com/that-time-macklemore-stole-thrift-shop-from-a-queer-new-york-rapper-20130827 }}
- {{cite web |title=Queer Rapper Le1f Lashes Out At Macklemore, Claims "Thrift Shop" Is His Stolen Song |author=Higbee, Jonathan |date=August 27, 2013 |website=Instinct |url=http://instinctmagazine.com/post/queer-rapper-le1f-lashes-out-macklemore-claims-thrift-shop-his-stolen-song |access-date=July 10, 2015 |archive-date=March 4, 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304131520/http://instinctmagazine.com/post/queer-rapper-le1f-lashes-out-macklemore-claims-thrift-shop-his-stolen-song |url-status=dead }} Some thrift shops have reported an increase in business, especially among college students, which they have attributed to the song.{{cite news |title='Thrift Shop' opens students' eyes to retail alternatives |first=Bridjet |last=Mendyuk |url=http://www.bgnews.com/entertainment/thrift-shop-opens-students-eyes-to-retail-alternatives/article_8ecced04-8233-11e2-a242-0019bb2963f4.html |newspaper=[[BG News]] |date=March 1, 2013 |access-date=March 3, 2013}}
- {{cite news |title=A 'Thrift Shop' Bump For Greeley Thrift Shops? |first=Emily |last=Boyer |url=http://www.kunc.org/post/thrift-shop-bump-greeley-thrift-shops |publisher=[[KUNC]] |date=March 1, 2013 |access-date=March 3, 2013}}
- {{cite news |title=Thrift stores provide budget-friendly fashions |first=Lauren |last=Cappelloni |url=http://www.udreview.com/thrift-stores-provide-budget-friendly-fashions-1.2998597 |newspaper=The Review |date=February 25, 2013 |access-date=3 March 2013}} Several locations that were used in the music video and those that are located in the general vicinity of the places used for filming reported that their sales had not seen a sizable bump, but there was "attention."{{cite news |title=Macklemore's "Thrift Shop" Has Had No Effect On Actual Thrift Shop Revenues |first=Maya |last=Shwayder |url= http://www.ibtimes.com/macklemores-thrift-shop-has-had-no-effect-actual-thrift-shop-revenues-1114394 |newspaper=International Business Times |date=March 6, 2013 |access-date=August 25, 2013}}

In August 2013, the rapper Le1f publicly criticized Macklemore's song on Twitter, claiming that "Thrift Shop" borrowed its beat extensively from his own earlier song, "Wut".

Some thrift shops have reported an increase in business, especially among college students, which they have attributed to the song. Several locations that were used in the music video and those that are located in the general vicinity of the places used for filming reported that their sales had not seen a sizable bump, but there was "attention."

sections.heading: Music video

The accompanying music video was co-directed by [[Jon Jon Augustavo]], Macklemore and Ryan Lewis. It was released on Lewis' YouTube channel on August 29, 2012.{{cite web|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=QK8mJJJvaes |title=Macklemore & Ryan Lewis – Thrift Shop Feat. sections.text: The accompanying music video was co-directed by Jon Jon Augustavo, Macklemore and Ryan Lewis. It was released on Lewis' YouTube channel on August 29, 2012. Filming took place at several thrift shops in Seattle, including Goodwill Outlet, Value Village in Capitol Hill, Red Light Vintage and Fremont Vintage Mall, as well as at Seattle locations like the Unicorn/Narwhal Arcade Bar and the Northwest African American Museum. Macklemore attempted to persuade a fellow Seattle rapper, Sir Mix-a-Lot, to appear in the video but he did not return the calls. Some local Seattle musicians like Thomas Grey of Champagne Champagne appear in the music video, and a DeLorean is shown as well. The video was nominated at the 2013 MTV Video Music Awards for Video of the Year.

sections.wikitext: [[Postmodern Jukebox]] covered the song in 2013, with [[Robyn Adele Anderson]] singing in a [[Roaring Twenties]] jazz style. The video went viral and boosted the career of Postmodern Jukebox. The video gathered four million views in its first year.<ref name="SonicScoop The Making">{{cite news |author1=Colletti |first=Justin |date=8 January 2015 |title=Postmodern Jukebox: The Making of a Multi-Million View YouTube Music Channel |publisher=SonicScoop |url=http://www.sonicscoop.com/2015/01/08/postmodern-jukebox-the-making-of-a-multi-million-view-youtube-music-channel/ |access-date=9 April 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160409225122/http://www.sonicscoop.com/2015/01/08/postmodern-jukebox-the-making-of-a-multi-million-view-youtube-music-channel/ |archive-date=9 April 2016}}</ref>

sections.heading: Parodies
sections.wikitext:
The children's show ''[[Sesame Street]]'' makes a parody of "Thrift Shop" in which Macklemore appeared playing the character "Mucklemore", shows [[Oscar the Grouch]] and his other Grouches the proper way to recycle their trash.<ref>{{cite magazine|url=https://www.billboard.com/music/pop/ed-sheeran-macklemore-stroll-down-sesame-street-exclusive-behind-5800472/|title=Ed Sheeran & Macklemore Stroll Down 'Sesame Street': Exclusive Behind-the-Scenes Video | date=November 12, 2013 | last=Payne | first=Chris | magazine=Billboard | access-date=January 29, 2023}}</ref>

In 2013, KIDZ BOP covered the song as part of their 24th album. The cover changes many of the original lyrics in order to make it appropriate for children to listen to.<ref>{{Cite AV media |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?feature=shared&v=HdDnSn9AlWM |title=Thrift Shop |date=2018-12-12 |last=KIDZ BOP Kids - Topic |access-date=2025-01-18 |via=YouTube}}</ref> 
 
A parody was part of a Pessach Shop Passover Jam, done for the Jewish holiday of [[Passover]] by the ''[[a cappella]]'' group Six13.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.gruntig.net/2013/03/six13-pesach-shop-2013-passover-jam.html |title=Six13 – Pesach Shop (2013 Passover Jam) |website=Gruntig.net |date=March 20, 2013 |access-date=September 24, 2016}}</ref>

The American comedy artist [[Rucka Rucka Ali]] parodied the song twice in his album ''[[Black Man of Steal]]''. One of his parodies is titled "I'm [[Barack Obama|Obama]]", the other, "I'm [[Osama bin Laden|Osama]]".<ref>Archived at [https://ghostarchive.org/varchive/youtube/20211205/Rw4BCniDqD0 Ghostarchive]{{cbignore}} and the [https://web.archive.org/web/20130324024510/http://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Rw4BCniDqD0&gl=US&hl=en Wayback Machine]{{cbignore}}: {{cite web| url = https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Rw4BCniDqD0| title = Thrift Shop PARODY "I'm Obama" ~ Rucka Rucka Ali | website=YouTube| date = March 20, 2013 }}{{cbignore}}</ref><ref>Archived at [https://ghostarchive.org/varchive/youtube/20211205/8hWVSvzh9os Ghostarchive]{{cbignore}} and the [https://web.archive.org/web/20141006063413/https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=8hWVSvzh9os Wayback Machine]{{cbignore}}: {{cite web| url = https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=8hWVSvzh9os| title = I'm Osama – Rucka Rucka Ali | website=YouTube| date = May 31, 2013 }}{{cbignore}}</ref>

[[Verizon Wireless]] parodied the song in a 2016 holiday promotion, this time in a laundromat.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=_UGokNrZx_8|title=Verizon Pre Paid Song Laundry Shop|website=YouTube |date=November 17, 2016|access-date=December 5, 2016}}</ref>

American parody web show "The Hillywood Show" samples the music in its parody of British TV show [[Sherlock (TV series)|Sherlock]], as well as reenacting some scenes from the music video.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ArdWL2uKf7k|title=Sherlock Parody by The Hillywood Show®|website=YouTube |date=August 20, 2016|access-date=January 7, 2023}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=LLTjkpQI1PE|title=Sherlock Parody Hillywood side-by-side comparison|website=YouTube |date=September 21, 2016|access-date=January 7, 2023}}</ref>

sections.heading: Media
sections.wikitext:
The song was also used in the trailers for the films ''[[Pain & Gain]]'', ''[[The Internship]]'' and ''[[Tammy (film)|Tammy]]''.{{Citation needed|date=November 2017}}

[["Weird Al" Yankovic]] recorded a cover version of "Thrift Shop" as part of his polka medley "[[List of "Weird Al" Yankovic polka medleys#"NOW That's What I Call Polka!"|NOW That's What I Call Polka!]]" for his 2014 album ''[[Mandatory Fun]]''.<ref name="LinerNotes">''Mandatory Fun'' liner notes</ref>

In 2018, a slightly modified version of the original song was also used for [[Suncorp]] advertisements featuring their mascot, Sunny.<ref name = "Suncorp ad 1 (2018)">Suncorp advertisement Are you ready to money with Sunny? https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=MZIIjUpH4VM</ref><ref name = "Suncorp Home Insurance ad 2018">Suncorp Home Insurance https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=rOFrp6sPx2k</ref><ref name = "Suncorp Sunny Growth saver ad 2018">Suncorp – Sunny Growth Saver https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=37IARE9ENfE</ref>

A censored version of the song is featured in the video game ''[[Just Dance 2026 Edition]]''. The map is fittingly set in a thrift store with the coach being a character named Dr. Vintz, who bears a resemblance to Macklemore from the original music video.
sections.text:
The song was also used in the trailers for the films Pain & Gain, The Internship and Tammy.{{Citation needed|date=November 2017}}

"Weird Al" Yankovic recorded a cover version of "Thrift Shop" as part of his polka medley "NOW That's What I Call Polka!" for his 2014 album Mandatory Fun.

In 2018, a slightly modified version of the original song was also used for Suncorp advertisements featuring their mascot, Sunny.

A censored version of the song is featured in the video game Just Dance 2026 Edition. The map is fittingly set in a thrift store with the coach being a character named Dr. Vintz, who bears a resemblance to Macklemore from the original music video.
